key_insight: A versatile two-layer model (VTLM) can replace full 3D microchannel heat-sink simulations with coupled 2D fields while still capturing key thermohydraulic effects.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster design tool for screening many microchannel geometries and operating conditions without explicitly resolving the channel-height direction.
method: Maps the 3D conjugate heat-transfer problem to two coupled 2D fields.
Uses hydraulic and thermal closure relations to represent wall friction and interlayer heat transfer.
Calibrates closures from representative channel geometry, flow-development state, and fin configuration.
evidence_signal: The VTLM was evaluated against 3D reference models over broad ranges of channel aspect ratio, operating condition, and fin arrangement, and it showed improved agreement over prior two-layer models.
watch_item: Accuracy depends strongly on flow-development condition and channel aspect ratio, so the conservative screening guideline should be checked before using the model outside the examined configurations.
paper_title: Versatile two-layer model for thermohydraulic prediction of microchannel heat sinks
